a:r.a:t: G-proteins mediate signal transduction from GPCRs to other target proteins.

p:cNvPr.descr: A diagram that illustrates four general types of signal transducers in the cell membrane. A large yellow background has a double blue line along the top edge. In between the double line is an even darker yellow labeled plasma membrane. The lower right corner of the diagram has a blue blackground with a dashed blue line along the top edge labeled nuclear envelope. Diagrams 1 to 3 represent signal transducers positioned along the plasma membrane. Diagram 1. A receptor, represented by an orange indented rectangular structure, labeled R, sits on the plasma membrane. To the right, there is a reversible arrow that has a gray circle with the letter, L inside of it. To the right of the reversible arrow is the same orange structure described previously attached to the gray circle with L in it; the circle sits on top of the R on the orange structure. To the bottom left of the orange structure, there's a green leaf-like structure connected that has the letter G on it. To the right of the green structure is an arrow pointed to the right, at another G structure that has hairlike projections all around. To the top right of this structure, a blue toothlike shape with hairlike projections around it is connected (it sits on top of the plasma membrane). This blue structure is labeled Enz, and has a downward facing arrow pointing away from its bottom; the arrow points to an X. The text accompanying Diagram 1 reads, ""G protein-couple receptor. External ligand binding to receptor activates an intracellular GTP-binding protein, which regulates an enzyme that generates an intracellular second messenger."" Diagram 2a. An image representing tyrosine kinase looks like two pink microphones connected at the head; each side has a dark pink projection at the bottom that rounds out into a blue circle and enters the yellow background space. To the top right of this is the same gray circle with an L described in diagram 1. Next to the tyrosine kinase structure on the plasma membrane is a reversible arrow. To the right of that is the same tyrosine kinase structure described previously, but the gray circle is bonded to the left head of the shape, and the blue circles at the bottom have hairlike projections all around them. The text accompanying this image reads, ""Receptor enzyme (tyrosine kinase). Ligand binding activate tyrosine kinase activity by autophophorylation."" An arrow points away from this shape (below it) to text that reads ""Kinase cascade."" This is the beginning of Diagram 2b. Another arrow points from the text to a brown circle that has a T in it. From this brown circle, another long, curved arrow points to the bottom left into the blue area below the nuclear envelope, to another brown circle with a T in it. This brown circle sits on top of a wave of dark and light blue double helices labeled DNA. On top of that is an arrow that point up and then to the right to a green wavy arrow labeled mRNA. On top of that, a black curved arrow points to the text, ""Protein,"" above and to the right. The text accompanying this diagram reads, ""Kinase activates transcription factor (T), altering gene expression."" Diagram 3 shows two purple structures that appear folded slightly inward. The first one is slightly skinnier because the fold is more drastic. To the top left is the same gray circle with an L, as described previously. To the right is a reversible arrow on the plasma membrane, and to the right of that is the second purple structure, less folded, with an arrow down its center into the yellow space. The gray circle with the L sits directly on top of this purple structure, on the left. Text accompanying diagram 3 reads, ""Gated ion channel. Channel opens or closes in response to concentration of signal ligand or membrane potential. A few spaces down, there is another gray circle with an L, and a dashed curved arrow pointing away from it to the left, to a tan oval with a gray circle in it. This gray circle also has an L in it. The tan oval sits on top of the same DNA, mRNA, and protein structures described in 2b. Text to the left reads, ""Nuclear receptor. Hormone binding allows the receptor to regulate the expression of specific genes."
